title: Support Complementarity
body_html:
Support Complementarity

Let $x \in X(A)$ and $y \in Y(A)$. If $i \in \operatorname{supp}(x)$, then the pure row $i$ obtains the value against $y$. If $j \in \operatorname{supp}(y)$, then the mixed strategy $x$ obtains the value against the pure column $j$.
proof_html:
Let $v=\operatorname{val}(A)$. Since $y$ is optimal for player $2$, each pure row payoff satisfies $e_iAy\le v$. Since $x$ is optimal for player $1$, the average of these row payoffs under $x$ is $$ xAy=\sum_i x_i(e_iAy)=v. $$ An average of numbers all bounded above by $v$ can equal $v$ only if every term with positive weight is equal to $v$. Hence $e_iAy=v$ for $i\in\operatorname{supp}(x)$. The column statement is dual: optimality of $x$ gives $xAe_j\ge v$ for every $j$, while optimality of $y$ gives $$ xAy=\sum_j y_j(xAe_j)=v. $$ Thus every positively weighted column in $y$ satisfies $xAe_j=v$.

References

  • [MFoGT, Prop. 2.4.1(b)] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MechDesign.pdf. Complementarity on supports of optimal strategies.
